transcript.text: t/d keeps cutting out after 10 mins then starts again if i leave it. vent hose goes out the window. pls help

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. This pattern—running for a short while then stopping—is classic overheating protection. The dryer detects it's getting too hot (often because airflow is restricted) and cuts power to prevent damage. It starts again once it cools down. The most common cause is a blockage in the air path, even if the hose looks okay from the outside. Fluff can build up inside the ducting or on the internal components. Please do these two quick checks:
1. Clean the lint filter thoroughly. If your model has a second filter (often at the bottom front behind a flap), remove and rinse that too under warm water, then let it dry completely before refitting.
2. Check the vent hose going out the window. Ensure it is not squashed, kinked, or blocked by debris. Detach it if possible and check for fluff buildup inside. If these are clear and the problem persists, we'll look at whether the internal fan is working or if a sensor is misreading dryness.
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
ok did the filter, clean. the hose is squashed behind it tho, i pushed the dryer back further recently. full of fluff in the folds. also the cabinet gets really hot before it stops

That explains it perfectly. A squashed hose full of fluff is a major blockage. The dryer can't get rid of hot, moist air, so it overheats and cuts out to protect itself. 1. Pull the dryer back carefully (you may need help as they are heavy) and straighten the vent hose so there are no kinks or squashes.
2. Detach the hose from the dryer and blow through it or use a vacuum to remove all fluff from inside.
3. Check the outside wall vent cover to make sure it opens freely and isn't blocked by debris. Once you've done that, put everything back together and run a test cycle. If it runs for more than 10 minutes without stopping, the problem is solved. Let me know if it still cuts out after clearing the hose.
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
ok will sort the hose and try again. i can try running it with the hose off the window too if that helps?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. I wouldn't recommend running it with the hose detached from the window. While that might let it run longer by removing back-pressure, it will pump moist air into your room which can cause dampness and mould issues, and it's not how the machine is designed to operate. The priority is getting that vent path clear so the hot air can escape properly. Once you've pulled the dryer back, straightened the hose, and vacuumed out all the fluff from inside it (and checked the wall vent outside opens freely), please put everything back together and run a test cycle. Understood. Take your time to get that hose clear—just remember to unplug the machine before you move it or touch the vent connection. Once you've reconnected everything, plug it back in and start a standard drying cycle with a normal load of laundry (don't run it empty). Stay nearby for the first 15 minutes. The key thing to watch is whether it still cuts out after about 10 minutes or if it keeps running smoothly once the airflow is restored. Let me know exactly what happens.
